title: Gluten-Free Vanilla Almond Flour Cupcakes
shortDescription: Fluffy gluten free vanilla cupcakes ready in 43 minutes, made with almond and tapioca flour for real lift.
description: These gluten free vanilla cupcakes are soft and fluffy, not gummy or dense like many almond flour bakes. I tested several ratios before landing on almond flour plus tapioca flour for real lift. Real vanilla extract gives these cupcakes a warm, rounded flavor. A little sour cream keeps the crumb moist without weighing it down. This recipe uses simple pantry staples, no gums or xanthan needed. It comes together in under 45 minutes, good for a quick gluten free treat any night of the week.
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Line a 12 cup muffin pan with paper liners.
Whisk almond flour, tapioca flour, coconut flour, baking powder, and salt in a medium bowl.
Beat butter and sugar in a large bowl until light and fluffy, about 2 minutes.
Add eggs one at a time, beating well after each. Mix in the vanilla extract.
Stir the sour cream into the wet mixture until smooth.
Add the dry mix in two batches, alternating with the milk. Mix just until combined, do not overbeat.
Divide batter evenly among liners, filling each about two-thirds full.
Bake 16 to 18 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool in the pan 5 minutes, then move to a rack.
tips: Weigh your almond flour if you can. Measuring by volume packs it down and makes cupcakes dense.
Do not overmix once the dry ingredients go in, or the tapioca flour can turn gummy.
Let eggs and butter sit out until room temperature for a smoother batter and better rise.
Cool cupcakes fully before frosting, gluten free crumbs are soft and can tear while warm.

faq.question: Why use tapioca flour with almond flour?
faq.answer: Tapioca flour adds lift and chew that almond flour cannot give alone, since almond flour has no gluten structure to trap air.

faq.question: Can I use almond meal instead of almond flour?
faq.answer: Fine ground almond flour works best here. Almond meal is coarser and makes the cupcakes heavier and more crumbly.

faq.question: Why did my cupcakes sink in the middle?
faq.answer: This usually means underbaking or too much liquid. Test with a toothpick at 16 minutes and measure your milk carefully.

faq.question: Can I make these dairy-free too?
faq.answer: Yes. Swap the butter for a plant-based baking stick and use a dairy-free sour cream in the same amount.

conclusion: This batter proves gluten free cupcakes can still be light and fluffy. Keep the almond to tapioca ratio as written and you will get a tender crumb every time. Frost with a simple vanilla buttercream and these disappear fast.
